description: Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. The National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) tracked and evaluated climate-related events that had great economic and societal impacts in the U.S. and across the globe from 1980 through 2024. Disaster categories tracked in the tool were: Users can explore billion-dollar disasters by state or county in interactive maps and graphs. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Extreme Cold, Flooding – General, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds, Severe Winter Weather, Wildfire. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Economy, People, Property, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
